label: rem:vector-meson-nonet
title: The vector nonet: singlet–octet mixing is the content-bearing target
html:
Remark. The vector nonet: singlet–octet mixing is the content-bearing target

The pseudoscalar octet of the meson-octet proposition is one of two nonets with identical \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} content. The other is the vector nonet 1^- --- \rho, K^*, \omega, \phi --- obtained from the same \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1} with the quark spins aligned rather than anti-aligned. The two nonets mix their octet and singlet almost oppositely, and no \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}-symmetric statement distinguishes them. That makes the mixing the first eightfold-way quantity whose derivation would carry information.

The contrast

Reported as quark content rather than as a mixing angle: angle conventions differ across the literature (\theta_V \approx 39^\circ and \approx 51^\circ are the same physics read two ways), whereas the s\bar{s} probability of the heavy state is convention-independent, and ideal mixing is exactly 1.

Nonet Heavy state s\bar{s} purity Departure from ideal
pseudoscalar 0^- \eta' 50.3\% 49.7 pp
vector 1^- \phi \mathbf{99.5\%} \mathbf{0.5} pp

The vector nonet is ideally mixed --- the \phi is s\bar{s} to within half a percentage point --- while the pseudoscalar nonet sits about as far from ideal as it can. Values from nonet-mixing-purity.witness.json; PDG central values are comparators, and nothing here is fitted.

This is also why Gell-Mann--Okubo appears to fail on the vector nonet. Applied to the physical states, the relation deviates by \approx 6\% for the pseudoscalar \eta but by \approx 32\% for the physical \omega. The discrepancy is not a failure of \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}: it is that the physical \omega is not the octet member at all, because the nonet is ideally mixed.

Why this target is different

The GMO relation is an identity of the first-order octet-breaking ansatz: it holds for every choice of the breaking parameters, so reproducing it is evidence for nothing. The decuplet equal-spacing rule behind the \Omega^- prediction is the same (QOU/Eightfold/DecupletEqualSpacing.lean, established later in this chapter).

The mixing is the opposite case, and this too is a theorem (QOU/Eightfold/NonetMixingUnconstrained.lean, sorry-free). Holding fixed the octet member m_8 that Gell-Mann--Okubo determines, every pair of physical masses is realisable by choosing the singlet entry and the octet--singlet mixing:

  m_1^2 = \lambda_1 + \lambda_2 - m_8^2,
  \qquad
  e^2 = (m_8^2 - \lambda_1)(\lambda_2 - m_8^2),

whereupon the characteristic polynomial is exactly (x - \lambda_1)(x - \lambda_2). The ansatz therefore constrains the mixing not at all, and the observed value is genuinely extra data. Setting e = 0 recovers the unmixed states, so the mixing is carried entirely by that one parameter --- the parameter on which the two nonets disagree.

Availability of the nonet in the framework

Open, and not currently attemptable. The nonet needs the singlet, which is unavailable at \dim V = 2: the alternating channel vanishes below N = 3 (RowCapObstruction.lean), so the \eta' and its vector counterpart do not exist framework-side. The vector nonet therefore inherits the N = 3 problem of the open-problems ledger in full.

What is recorded here is a statement about the target, not about prospects. Of the eightfold way's three headline quantitative successes, two are now proved content-free as derivation targets and this one is proved content-bearing, which makes its derivation the highest-value open item in this chapter.

In QCD the near-ideal vector mixing is attributed to the OZI (quark-line) rule, and the pseudoscalar departure from it to the axial anomaly. The framework has no account of either, and no candidate mechanism is proposed here.
